READING

Breakfast around the world

1
Discuss these questions.
What’s the most important meal of the day for you – breakfast, lunch or dinner? Why?
For me, breakfast is the most important meal because if I skip it, I feel tired and can’t concentrate well.
What time do you usually have each meal?
I usually have breakfast at about eight, lunch around one and dinner at seven or eight.
Do you eat any snacks between meals? What?
Yes. I often have fruit, yoghurt or a sandwich between meals.

Read the article about breakfast around the world and match each photo to a country. One country does not have a photo. Name the food and dishes you see.
They say breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Maybe that's why many people may be open to trying foreign food at lunch or dinner, but they're not adventurous enough to experimentэкспериментировать with anything new at breakfast. But what about you? Below, we look at typicalтипичный breakfasts in five different countries. Would you have them at home or are they too spicy, too fattening or just too different?

South Korea

The traditional breakfast is rice and soup. People then choose extra dishes to go with it such as grilled fishрыба на гриле, vegetablesовощи and kimchiкимчхи, острая маринованная капуста, which is pickled cabbageмаринованная капуста with chillies. Kimchi is so popular that the first Korean astronaut took some with him to the International Space Station! Of course, these days, many Koreans have such busy lifestylesнапряжённый образ жизни they don’t have enough time to make breakfast and just grabсхватить / быстро взять / перехватить a quick coffee and some cerealхлопья or toast.

Bulgaria

Breakfast in Bulgaria includesвключает tea or strong coffee, sesame bread and butter, cheese made from sheep's milkовечье молоко, honey, olives, boiled eggs and – most importantly – a local yoghurtйогурт. Bulgaria has a lot of people aged over 100 and many believe that the secretсекрет behind this is their yoghurt, which most Bulgarians eat every day.

Costa Rica

Many Costa Ricans start their day with the national dishнациональное блюдо, gallo pintoгалло пинто, which is a mixture of fried riceжареный рис and black beansчёрная фасоль. It’s lightly spiced and often served with fried plantainжареный плантан (овощной банан), cream and fried eggs. There’s usually some strong local coffee as well – or perhaps some agua dulceagua dulce, сладкий напиток из сахарного тростника, which is made from sugar cane juice.

Egypt

Visit any town in Egypt in the morning and you’ll find street stallsуличные ларьки / палатки selling foul medammesфуль медаммес – beans cooked with tomatoes and onions – and eaten with a boiled egg on top and lots of flat breadлепёшка / плоский хлеб. Pickled vegetables are usually served as a side dishгарнир. For many poorer Egyptians, this is their only food until dinner. They say the dish is ‘a rock in the stomach«камень в желудке»’.

Ireland

As people become more concerned aboutобеспокоены / озабочены their health, fewer Irish eat the traditional Irish breakfastтрадиционный ирландский завтрак, or fryжареный завтрак / fry-up, because it has too much fatжир. However, many still eat it if they stay in a hotel, but they cook it on a special day. It consists ofсостоит из bacon, black puddingкровяная колбаса (a kind of sausage made with blood), white puddingбелая колбаса (another kind of sausage), fried eggs, fried mushrooms and toast – all served with strong Irish tea!

GRAMMAR

too and not … enough

too and not … enough

We use too or not … enough to show there is a problem.

We use too when we need less of something, and not … enough when we need more of something.

GR
Grammar reference: TOO / NOT … ENOUGH

tooслишком, too muchслишком много (неисчисляемое), too manyслишком много (исчисляемое)

Use too + adjective / adverb when you want / need less of something. It is often followed by the infinitive with to to show something is not possible as a result.

I’m too lazy to cook for myself.
He was driving too fast to stop in time.

Use too much + uncountable noun or too many + countable noun.

My doctor says I’m eating too much sugar.
Too many people these days eat fast food.

not … enough

Use not + adjective / adverb + enough when you need more. It is also often followed by the infinitive with to.

My daughter helps me cook, but she’s not old enough to be left on her own in the kitchen.
You didn’t cook it long enough. It’s still raw in the centre.

Use not enough + noun (either uncountable or countable).

They’re closing down the restaurant on the corner, because it doesn’t make enough money.
The match was cancelled because we didn’t have enough people to make a team.

Questions
You can use enough in questions. It means ‘is it OK or is more needed?’
Do you have enough food?
Are you comfortable enough?

2 It’s been cooked long. Look, it’s almost burnt!
3 Are you warm ?
4 Have you had dessert?
5 I think we made food. People haven’t eaten a lot.

Responses a–h

a Yes thanks. It was lovely. Shall I help you clear the table?
b Actually, no. Could we sit inside instead?
c You’re probably right. Shall we ask the waiter to cancel a couple?
d We don’t actually. Could you bring a couple of folding ones?

f Not really. Could you turn it up?
g Oh yes. Shall I ask the waiter to change it?

CM
COMMON MISTAKES

Enough goes after an adjective / adverb, but before a noun.

I am not enough patient enough to be a teacher.
I am not patient enough to be a teacher.

I don’t have money enough enough money to eat out every week.
I don’t have enough money to eat out every week.

Don’t use too to describe positive feelings. Too means you want less. Use really / very / so and an adjective like great, fantastic or amazing.

I love my Mum’s cooking too much. She’s too good. I miss it now I live on my own.
I really love my Mum’s cooking. She’s fantastic.

You don’t need for before an infinitive with to.

Leave it to cool down. It’s too hot for to eat now.
Leave it to cool down. It’s too hot to eat now.

SPEAKING

Using too / not enough

6
Use too / not … enough to complain about the things in the box. Say what you would do to solve the problem.
a coffeea hotela meala rooma cara jacketa moviea steak
Example: It’s too hot to drink. Leave it to cool. · It’s too weak for my liking. Leave it for a bit longer. · It’s too bitter. Add some sugar.
1 a coffee
It’s too hot to drink. Leave it to cool. / It’s too weak for my liking. Leave it for a bit longer.
2 a hotel
It’s too noisy to sleep in. Ask for another room. / It’s not clean enough. Complain at reception.
3 a meal
It’s too salty. Send it back. / It’s not hot enough. Ask them to heat it up.
4 a room
It’s too small for all of us. We need a bigger one. / It isn’t warm enough. Turn the heating on.
5 a car
It’s too expensive to buy. Look for a cheaper one. / It isn’t big enough for the family.
6 a jacket
It’s too tight to wear comfortably. Try a bigger size. / It isn’t warm enough for winter.
7 a movie
It’s too long to watch tonight. Let’s watch something shorter. / It isn’t funny enough.
8 a steak
It’s too raw. Ask them to cook it a bit more. / It’s too tough to eat easily.

SOUNDS AND VOCABULARY REVIEW

Review and pronunciation

8
Listen and repeat the sounds with /v/, /b/, /f/ and /p/. Are any of them difficult to hear or say?
Original Track 22 embedded.
/vjuː/ · /ɜːv/ · /fɪ/ · /bɪ/ · /pɪ/ · /bʊ/ · /pɔː/ · /fæ/ · /feɪ/ · /ve/ · /və/ · /pɑː/
Pronunciation practice: listen once without repeating, then replay and copy each sound chunk. Pay special attention to the contrast between /v/ and /f/, and between /b/ and /p/.

/v/

Voice on. Top teeth touch the lower lip.

/f/

Same mouth position as /v/, but no voice.

/b/

Both lips close; voice on.

/p/

Both lips close; no voice and a small puff of air.
